question: A recently published study suggests that the Italian Mafia has adapted its scams to skim money off the EU budget. It further states that EU projects worth less than EUR 150 000 are specifically targeted, as the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF), the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) and other Commission departments do not see cases of this size to be worth prosecuting1.
Organised crime is thus deliberately exploiting thresholds and de minimis limits to operate under the radar of watchdogs and law enforcement. 1.

Is the Commission willing to corroborate the findings of this study, namely that organised crime favours EU projects worth less than EUR 150 000 because OLAF, the EPPO and other Commission departments consider such cases to be too insignificant to prosecute?
What conclusions does the Commission intend to draw from these findings, particularly with regard to existing de minimis and minor offence thresholds in the fight against fraud?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.9.2026) Regulation (EU, Euratom) 883/20131 does not establish a financial threshold for the opening of an investigation by the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF). In its independent investigations, OLAF assesses each case individually based on the criteria set out in Article 5(1) of Regulation (EU, Euratom) 883/2013 and not only based on its possible financial impact.

The European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) investigates and prosecutes – in full independence from the Commission and all other EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies – crimes affecting the EU’s financial interests (Protection of the European Union’s Financial Interests – PIF crimes), including organised crime when the focus of the activity of criminal organisations is to commit PIF crimes.

The 2025 EPPO Annual Report2 demonstrates the key role played by the EPPO in dismantling criminal organisations. In 2025, organised crime cases accounted for about 15% of the total EPPO cases (529 out of 3 602). The threshold of EUR 150 000 referred to in the text of the question does not affect the competence of the EPPO or OLAF to open or conduct investigations.
